findings.title: The service exits immediately after starting
findings.description: main starts the janitor, prints the listening message, and immediately returns. Returning from main terminates the process, so the service never remains available to handle requests.

findings.title: Missing Authorization headers cause undefined behavior
findings.description: bearer_token adds one to the null pointer returned by strchr when the header contains no space. handle calls this function with an empty string when the header is absent, so an ordinary unauthenticated request can crash instead of returning 401.

findings.title: Link expiration logic is inverted
findings.description: resolve erases and rejects a link while the current time is before its expiration. Consequently newly created live links fail immediately, while already-expired links are resolved and counted.

findings.title: Partial pages construct an out-of-bounds iterator
findings.description: When the requested end exceeds the number of links, end is set to all.size() + 1. For example, the report endpoint requests 1000 items from a one-item store and then constructs a vector using an iterator beyond one-past-the-end, causing undefined behavior.

findings.title: Stats crashes when the store is empty
findings.description: total_hits is divided by g_store->size() without checking for zero. Requesting /stats before any links exist performs integer division by zero.

findings.title: Missing request parameters terminate request handling
findings.description: Handlers use map::at for required query parameters without validating their presence or catching out_of_range. Malformed requests to create, redirect, delete, or out therefore throw instead of returning a client error.

findings.title: Janitor increments an invalidated iterator
findings.description: Erasing the current map element invalidates it, but the for loop subsequently increments that invalid iterator. Encountering an expired link can therefore crash the janitor or skip/corrupt traversal.

findings.title: Cache sweep increments an invalidated iterator
findings.description: sweep erases its current map iterator and then lets the loop increment the invalid iterator. Any sweep containing an expired entry has undefined behavior.

findings.title: Renaming a link uses a dangling reference
findings.description: rename binds a reference to the map value, erases the owning map node, and then reads and modifies the destroyed Link through that reference. Renaming an existing link has undefined behavior.

findings.title: Target checking always reads past the vector
findings.description: The loop condition uses i <= links.size(). Empty input is indexed immediately, and an all-valid nonempty input is indexed once at links.size(), causing undefined behavior.

findings.title: format_row returns a pointer to destroyed storage
findings.description: row is a local stack array, so the returned pointer becomes dangling as soon as format_row returns. Reading the formatted row subsequently has undefined behavior.

findings.title: Snapshot replacement can silently fail or publish incomplete data
findings.description: The temporary file is outside the destination directory, remains buffered and open during rename, and rename's result is ignored. Cross-filesystem renames can fail outright, while a crash after rename but before the stream flushes can replace the prior snapshot with incomplete data.

findings.title: Cache entries leak on every removal or replacement
findings.description: Entries are allocated with new, but expiration, eviction, erase, replacement, and the destructor remove only their map pointers. Cache churn therefore causes unbounded heap growth.

findings.title: Cache eviction is not least-recently-used
findings.description: Although accesses update Entry::used, set always evicts entries_.begin(), which is merely the lexicographically smallest code. Frequently used entries can be discarded while stale ones remain.

findings.title: A zero-sized cache erases an invalid iterator
findings.description: Configuration permits cache_size to be zero. In that case set enters the full-cache branch while entries_ is empty and passes entries_.end() to erase, which is undefined behavior.

findings.title: Cache utilization is truncated and can divide by zero
findings.description: Integer division occurs before multiplication, so every partially filled cache reports 0%. A configured limit of zero also causes division by zero when /stats is requested.

findings.title: peek reports expired entries as cached
findings.description: peek checks only whether a map key exists and ignores the entry's expiration time. Until a get or sweep removes it, callers receive true for data that the cache itself considers expired.

findings.title: Millisecond configuration values are interpreted as seconds
findings.description: LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS and LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS are documented as milliseconds but are directly used to construct Seconds. A value of 1000 therefore becomes 1000 seconds instead of one second.

findings.title: Invalid timeout replaces the default despite the diagnostic
findings.description: When LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS parses to zero, the code says it is keeping the default but unconditionally assigns Seconds{0}. The resulting configuration contradicts the diagnostic and is unusable.

findings.title: LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT is parsed and discarded
findings.description: A positive environment value is stored only in a local variable and never assigned to cfg.fetch_limit. Deployments setting the option silently continue using the default value of 32.

findings.title: Configuration validation always succeeds
findings.description: validate collects and prints fatal configuration problems but returns true unconditionally. Moreover, main ignores the result, so invalid ports, sizes, or timeouts do not prevent startup as promised.

findings.title: Unnamed reports are read back from the wrong file
findings.description: export_csv substitutes the default name "links" when name is empty, but report passes the original empty name to read_report. A report request without a name writes links.csv and then reads .csv, returning an empty response.

findings.title: CSV fields are emitted without escaping
findings.description: Codes, targets, and owners are concatenated with commas and newlines without CSV quoting. A target or owner containing a comma, quote, or newline produces a structurally incorrect report.

findings.title: rename validates the source code twice
findings.description: The destination code is never passed to validate_code because the second call repeats from. rename can therefore insert codes that violate the Store's documented code constraints.

findings.title: Success rate is zero unless every link was used
findings.description: Integer division is performed before multiplying by 100. For any nonempty store where used is less than the total, used / links_.size() truncates to zero.

findings.title: Removing a link does not release its quota
findings.description: remove erases the link but never decrements quota_ for its owner. The recorded per-owner count remains permanently inflated, so deletion does not give the owner the promised quota slot back.

findings.title: top returns the least-used links and may invent entries
findings.description: The comparator sorts hits in ascending order, so truncation keeps the least-followed links. If n exceeds the number of links, resize also appends default-constructed Link objects that were never in the store.

findings.title: extend revives expired links
findings.description: The method unconditionally sets expiration relative to the current time. Calling it for an already-expired link makes that dead code live again, contrary to the stated final-expiry behavior.

findings.title: Batch import is not atomic
findings.description: Each link is inserted immediately after its own validation. If a later link is invalid and throws, all earlier links remain inserted, violating the method's all-or-nothing contract.

findings.title: prune increments an invalidated iterator
findings.description: prune erases the current map iterator and then increments it in the loop expression. Removing any expired entry causes undefined behavior and can crash or skip entries.

findings.title: prune returns the remaining size instead of the removal count
findings.description: The function tracks removed but returns links_.size(). Callers therefore receive the number of surviving links rather than the documented number removed.

findings.title: last_code returns a dangling string_view
findings.description: The returned string_view refers to the local string newest, which is destroyed when last_code returns. Any subsequent use of the view has undefined behavior.

findings.title: last_code chooses map order instead of creation order
findings.description: Iteration over std::map leaves newest equal to the lexicographically greatest code, not the most recently created link. The dashboard can therefore display an older code.

findings.title: Reading an unknown owner's count mutates the quota map
findings.description: operator[] inserts a zero-valued entry when the owner is absent. Merely querying an unknown owner therefore changes Store state and increases the owner count shown by admin_quotas.

findings.title: Redirect lookup changes valid uppercase codes
findings.description: The redirect handler lowercases every supplied code even though validate_code permits uppercase characters and Store keys are case-sensitive. Imported or renamed uppercase codes cannot be resolved through this endpoint.

findings.title: Store state is accessed concurrently without synchronization
findings.description: Request handlers and the janitor share the same Store, but none of its map or Link accesses are synchronized. Two redirects for one code can race on hits++, while create/remove/prune or the janitor can mutate links_ as another thread traverses or dereferences it. These interleavings are C++ data races and can lose updates, invalidate iterators, corrupt the map, or crash the process.

findings.title: Parallel cache operations race on entries and counters
findings.description: warm_cache launches multiple Cache::set calls concurrently, and the janitor concurrently calls sweep while other code can call get, set, or utilization. All of these touch entries_, Entry fields, or hits_ without synchronization. Overlapping writers can corrupt the std::map, and an erase can invalidate an iterator another operation is using.

findings.title: warm_cache destroys joinable threads and terminates the process
findings.description: The workers vector goes out of scope without joining or detaching any thread. For every nonempty input, destruction of its joinable std::thread objects invokes std::terminate, even if the worker functions have already finished.

findings.title: stop_janitor returns before the janitor has stopped
findings.description: stop_janitor only clears the atomic flag and never joins the thread. If the worker already evaluated the while condition and is sleeping, stop_janitor can return and the caller can destroy Store or Cache; the worker then wakes and executes one more sweep through dangling references. The heap-allocated thread object is also never reclaimed.

findings.title: Session lookup races with session insertion and revocation
findings.description: verify iterates sessions_ without synchronization while issue inserts and revoke erases from the same map. A concurrent revoke can invalidate the node being inspected or returned, and any overlapping map mutation and traversal is a data race with undefined behavior on the authentication path.

findings.title: Metrics counters race between request threads
findings.description: resolved_ and created_ are plain longs incremented by handlers and read by the stats handler without synchronization. Concurrent requests can perform overlapping read-modify-write operations, causing undefined behavior and lost counts; a stats request can also race with either increment.

findings.title: Concurrent snapshots share one temporary file
findings.description: Every snapshot writer uses /tmp/linkd-snapshot.json. If two calls overlap, one can truncate or overwrite the other's temporary contents; the first rename removes the shared pathname, causing the other rename to fail while its still-open stream may continue writing into the first destination. This can corrupt one snapshot and leave the other destination missing.

findings.title: Concurrent reports with the same name overwrite each other
findings.description: Two report requests using the same name open the same path with truncation and write without coordination. Their writes can overlap, and either request can read after the other has replaced the file, returning another request's snapshot or a partially overwritten report.

findings.title: Authorization header parsing permits unauthenticated memory corruption
findings.description: Every request reaches bearer_token before authentication. An Authorization header longer than 63 bytes overflows the 64-byte stack buffer through strcpy, while a missing header or one without a space makes space null and constructs a string from an invalid address. A remote unauthenticated client can therefore crash the process and may be able to execute code through the stack overwrite.

findings.title: Session tokens are generated with a predictable PRNG
findings.description: Bearer tokens are two outputs from std::rand, which is deterministic and is not seeded anywhere in scope. The same generator also produces observable link codes. An attacker who reconstructs the generator state can predict another user's token and authenticate as that user.

findings.title: Bearer tokens are written to application logs
findings.description: The complete session token is logged when issued. Anyone with access to console output or aggregated logs can copy the token and use it as the owner until it is revoked; the missing expiry check makes this exposure effectively permanent.

findings.title: Expired sessions remain valid indefinitely
findings.description: verify returns a matching session without comparing expires_at with the current time. A token stolen from logs, a client, or network telemetry continues authorizing every endpoint after its intended 12-hour lifetime.

findings.title: Any authenticated user can delete another user's links
findings.description: The DELETE /links handler removes the supplied code without comparing the link owner to the authenticated session. An authenticated attacker who learns or predicts another link code can permanently delete it.

findings.title: Caller-controlled header bypasses the admin authorization check
findings.description: The purportedly administrative /admin/quotas route trusts x-admin: true instead of the authenticated session's role. Any user with an ordinary valid token can add that header and access the admin response.

findings.title: Report names permit path traversal and arbitrary CSV-file overwrite
findings.description: The authenticated /report route inserts the request's name directly between the export directory and the .csv suffix. A name such as ../../../tmp/victim escapes the export directory, allowing the service account to truncate and overwrite any writable path ending in .csv.

findings.title: Report endpoint exposes every owner's links to ordinary users
findings.description: After checking only that some session exists, /report exports g_store->page rather than filtering by session.owner or requiring an administrator. Any authenticated account can retrieve other users' owner identifiers, targets, codes, and hit counts.

findings.title: Report pagination reads past the vector boundary
findings.description: When a requested page extends past a nonempty collection, end is set to all.size() + 1. /report always requests 1000 entries, so a normal store containing fewer than 1000 links constructs a vector using a past-the-end-plus-one iterator. An authenticated requester can trigger undefined behavior, including process termination or memory corruption.

findings.title: Unescaped CSV fields allow spreadsheet formula injection
findings.description: Owner and target values ultimately supplied by users are emitted without CSV escaping. An attacker can place a newline followed by a formula in the owner field so that a generated report executes attacker-controlled spreadsheet functions when support or another user opens it.

findings.title: Email tracking endpoint is an open redirect
findings.description: The /out endpoint copies an arbitrary next query value into Location without restricting its destination. An authenticated attacker can create a trusted linkd URL that redirects victims to a phishing or malware site, which is especially plausible because this endpoint is intended for links in email.

findings.title: Statistics endpoint can divide by zero
findings.description: When the store contains no links, /stats divides total_hits by size zero. An authenticated attacker can reach this state on a fresh service or after deleting the remaining links and then crash the process by requesting /stats.

findings.title: Link expiration check is reversed
findings.description: resolve deletes links while they are still valid but permits them once expires_at has passed. A caller who uses a supposedly expired code before the janitor removes it is redirected to its target, bypassing the expiry control for up to the janitor interval.
